tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. A Dictionary of the Jili (Migili) Language of Central Nigeria. Draft ms. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, rogerblench.info.
tone_statements.quote: 3.3 Tones Jili has three level tones, as the following minimal triplets show; bɛ́ to come / bɛ question particle / bɛ̀ to choose; ká ‘that he’ / ka to guard / kà to exceed. There are also numerous complex glide tones. These symbolised as follows; Rising: Low-High hachek over the syllable ˇ; Low-Mid; Mid-High ∆. Falling: High-Low circumflex over the syllable ˆ; High-Mid; Mid-Low. [...] [§4.2] Tones on pronouns change according to the TAM features of the clause in which they occur.
tone_statements.locator: §3.3 Tones, pp. 3-4 (minimal-triplet and glide tables linearized with ' / ' and ';'), and §4.2 Pronouns, p. 4
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + 6 glides (LH, LM, MH, HL, HM, ML)

tone.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L) + 6 glides (LH, LM, MH, HL, HM, ML)
tone.says: Three level tones (H, M, L) shown by minimal triplets (bɛ́ 'to come' / bɛ question particle / bɛ̀ 'to choose'; ká 'that he' / ka 'to guard' / kà 'to exceed'), plus 'numerous complex glide tones' (rising L-H, L-M, M-H; falling H-L, H-M, M-L) with an orthographic diacritic table; grammatical tone: 'Tones on pronouns change according to the TAM features of the clause'. Secondary to Stofberg 1978b but with Blench's own field emendations.

sources.note: No analysis: the Migili column carries phonetic tone diacritics (e.g. kūpɛ́lɛ́ 'stone') but the authors state 'there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features'; §1 remarks that the names [ūʤīʤīlí] vs [ūʤīʤīlī] 'only differ in tone on the last syllable' (about uji). Nothing on the Lijili tone system as such.
